append.text: **Ps 39:18b *Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es* → *Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu protetor*** (= 27:7's words; the pair with an agent noun again). The Latinist passed it twice this time; the stylist failed it ('an abstract noun beside a person-noun, the pair limps') and offered *socorro* / *amparo* — refused (*socorro* is as abstract; *amparo* is suscípere's, 39:12). **69:6b *Adjútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu* will copy the first half.**

**Ps 39:14b *Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice* → *Senhor, olhai para auxiliar-me*** (draft 1 *para me auxiliar* was heard 'look at me' by the stylist; the enclitic after the infinitive mends it). This is the half that Ps 69:2b shares (*Dómine, ad adjuvándum me festína*, the response of every Hour's opening versicle): it fixes *auxiliar-me* there, not *inténde in adjutórium* (D40, deferred). The stylist's *olhai em meu auxílio* refused: adjutórium's noun, and it would pre-empt D40.

**Ps 39:11b *a concílio multo* → *da congregação numerosa*: checked — ἀπὸ συναγωγῆς πολλῆς (Rahlfs, in the parallels).** D34's 'not yet checked' is closed. The stylist heard it 'administrative' and asked *assembleia* (ecclésia's, one verse before) — refused. multus → *numerosa*, not *grande* (magna, 39:10).
**Ps 39:3b *Et státuit super petram pedes meos* → *E firmou os meus pés sobre uma rocha*** (passed all three readers).
**Ps 39:3 *edúxit me de lacu misériæ* → *me tirou da cova da miséria*** — the *tirar de* of 29:4 and 30:5 where a source is named; passed all three readers.

**Ps 39:7 *aures autem perfecísti mihi* → *mas me aperfeiçoastes os ouvidos*** — passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'improved my hearing' (obedience not audible): the Latin's image, kept. Heb 10:5 (Clementine, fetched) has *corpus autem aptasti mihi* — another Latin, not followed.

**Ps 39:12 *ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me* → *não ponhais longe de mim as vossas compaixões*** (*longe fácere*, the same Greek μακρύνω as 21:20). The stylist called *pôr longe* a calque and asked *afastar*; refused (the Latin says *longe*).

**Ps 39:14 *Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me* → *Que vos agrade, Senhor, que me liberteis*** — the jussive as *Que vos agrade*, *ut* + subjunctive as a *que*-clause (draft 1's infinitive *libertar-me* rhymed with *auxiliar*). *Seja do vosso agrado* (MS1932) option. The Office of the Dead antiphon (Commune/C9) has *erípias*.
Ps 39:14 *ut éruas me* (no source) → *libertar* (*que me liberteis*), as 30:3.

**Ps 39:10 *lábia mea non prohibébo* → *não reterei os meus lábios*** — the blind reader heard 'I will not keep silent' (the sense); the stylist heard *re-te-rei* stutter and 'not idiomatic', asked *conterei* — refused for the row, noted as the second stylist to ask (after 33:14).

**Ps 39:15, 39:15b (×2) → *desonrados*, copying 34:4.** The Latinist (minor, twice) asked *confundidos* / *se envergonhem*: revereor is inner abashment, *desonrado* outer dishonour. Refused for the row and D15, but his point is evidence for the ruling: the row's word leans outward.

**Ps 39:16 copied: *os que me dizem: Que bom, que bom*.** The stylist ('sounds sincere and cheerful, not jeering') and the blind reader ('the mockery may be missed') both failed it; the stylist asked *Bem feito* again. Held for the row; the recurring complaint is noted for the ruling (69:4 still to copy).
Ps 39:5 *vanitátes et insánias falsas* → *as vaidades e as loucuras enganosas*: the blind reader heard conceit first again (the fourth psalm).
**Ps 39:2 *Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum* → *Aguardando, aguardei o Senhor*** (gerund + verb, the participle row; D39); passed all three readers, the stylist named it among the best.
**Ps 39:15 → *Sejam envergonhados e desonrados juntos, os que buscam a minha alma, * para tirá-la*** (+ *simul*, + *ut áuferant eam*; the comma after *juntos* is the stylist's).

**Ps 39:14 is not this formula**: *Compláceat tibi … ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice* has neither *inténde* nor *adjutórium*; it shares only *Dómine, ad adjuvándum me* with 69:2b (→ *auxiliar-me*, the adjuváre row). D40 stays open.

terms: | fæx (*lutum fæcis*) | borra (*e da lama da borra*) | open | Ps 39:3 only (ἰλύος; L&S 'dregs, sediment'). Draft 1 *da lama do lodo*: the Latinist and the stylist heard a tautology, the blind reader a doubled image — *borra* keeps the second noun and its image of foul sediment. *do lodo profundo* (MS1932) option. |

| carmen | canto (*um canto ao nosso Deus*) | open | Ps 39:4 only (ὕμνον). Kept one step from *cântico* (cánticum, same verse); *hino* is hymnus's (118:171), though the graduals that adapt this verse (Pent15-0, Quad4-2) read *hymnum*. Passed all readers. |

| insánia (*insániæ falsæ*) | loucura (*as loucuras enganosas*) | open | Ps 39:5 only (μανίας ψευδεῖς). Draft 1 *loucuras falsas* failed the stylist ('a madness is not false') and the blind reader (the lie inaudible); *enganosas* (MS1932) taken. The Latinist at the gate asked *falsas* back (minor) — held, option 2. dolus / dolósus keep *engano / enganador*. |

| oblátio | oferenda (*Não quisestes sacrifício nem oferenda*) | open | Ps 39:7, 50:21 (grep). *oblação* option (the liturgical cognate). Heb 10:5 Clementine has *Hostiam et oblationem* — another Latin. |

| *pro peccáto* (the sin offering, elliptic) | *oferta pelo pecado* (*nem oferta pelo pecado*) | open | Ps 39:7b (περὶ ἁμαρτίας). The Latinist asked the ellipsis *nem pelo pecado* twice (minor): refused, heard 'nor because of sin'. DRB 'sin offering'. |

| *in cápite libri* | na cabeça do livro | open | Ps 39:8 = Heb 10:7 (Clementine, fetched); the gradual verse of Epi1-0. The image kept as *caput ánguli*; the blind reader heard 'at the beginning of the book'. *No princípio do livro* option. |
| annuntiáre | anunciar | working | Ps 9:12, 9:15, 18:2, 21:32, 29:10b, 37:19, 39:6b, 39:10 — uniform; no row till now. |

| mendícus | mendigo (*Eu, porém, sou mendigo e pobre*) | open | Ps 39:18, 108:17 (grep); kept apart from pauper *pobre*, egénus *necessitado*, inops *carente* (D38). 69:6 has *egénus* where 39:18 has mendícus. |

| *sollícitus esse* (+ gen.) | ter cuidado de (*o Senhor tem cuidado de mim*) | open | Ps 39:18 only (φροντιεῖ). The cognate *solícito* is 'obliging' in Brazil. Passed all readers; the stylist's best line. |
| conféstim | logo (*Carreguem logo a sua vergonha*) | open | Ps 39:16 only; *depressa* is cito's. 69:4 has *statim* in the twin line. |

| *ferre confusiónem* | carregar a vergonha (*Carreguem logo a sua vergonha*) | open | Ps 39:16 (κομισάσθωσαν). *Levem* heard as 'take away'; *Suportem* (DRB) and *Sofram* (MS1932) options. Passed all readers. |
| tardáre (*ne tardáveris*) | tardar (*meu Deus, não tardeis*) | open | Ps 39:18b; 69:6b has morári (*ne moréris*) in the twin line → *demorar*, to stay apart. |
| auferre | tirar (*para tirá-la*) | working | Ps 9:26b, 118:22, 118:43, 39:15 (*ut áuferant eam*, the life). No row till now. |
| *super númerum* | além de todo número | open | Ps 39:6b (ὑπὲρ ἀριθμόν). The Latinist asked *além do número* twice (minor): not Portuguese; *todo* is the idiom's. *sem número* option. |
formulas: | *Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice* (39:14; the Office of the Dead Matins antiphon with *erípias*, Commune/C9; a versicle ending *festína*, Tempora/Epi2-2 — grep) | *Que vos agrade, Senhor, que me liberteis: * Senhor, olhai para auxiliar-me* | working (Ps 39) — its second half shares *ad adjuvándum me* with 69:2b (*festína*), not the D40 half |

| Ps 39:15b–18b ↔ Ps 69:4–6b (the doublet: *Convertántur / Avertántur retrórsum*, *qui volunt mihi mala*, *Euge, euge*, *Exsúltent et læténtur super / in te*, *Ego vero / autem … pauper*, *Adjútor meus … Dómine / Deus meus, ne moréris / tardáveris*) | 39's wordings: *Voltem para trás … os que me querem mal*; *Que bom, que bom*; *Exultem e alegrem-se em vós … e digam sempre os que amam a vossa salvação: Engrandecido seja o Senhor*; *Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu protetor* | working (Ps 39) — Ps 69 copies where the Latin agrees and decides locally where it differs (*erubéscant*, *statim erubescéntes*, *egénus*, *Deus, ádjuva me*, *liberátor*, *morári*) |

| *In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei* (39:8; Heb 10:7 in another Latin; the Epi1-0 gradual verse) | *Na cabeça do livro está escrito de mim que eu faça a vossa vontade: * meu Deus, eu quis, e a vossa lei no meio do meu coração* | working (Ps 39) — the second colon verbless as the Latin |
